analysis.headline: Stocks were mixed Wednesday (Dow down 561 points, or 1.1%, S&P 500 down about 0.2% for a fifth straight loss, Nasdaq up 0.4%), and futures are sharply higher this morning, led by Nasdaq 100 futures up about 2%, ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut.
analysis.summary: Wednesday's Dow drop was mostly health insurers: UnitedHealth fell about 10% and Humana about 13% as investors weighed a federal proposal to expand Medicare Advantage audits, while Nvidia gave back an early post-earnings gain and closed down about 2.9% despite revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier. Rate worries added pressure: minutes of the Fed's October meeting, released Wednesday afternoon, said almost all officials see further rate hikes as likely appropriate, with a couple open to more than a quarter point in December, and the 10-year Treasury yield was near 5.07%. That higher-for-longer outlook and a firm dollar pushed gold to about $3,725 an ounce, its weakest in more than a year, and Bitcoin fell about 3% to near $62,500, while WTI crude dropped about 3% to roughly $83 after a surprise build in U.S. crude stocks. This morning the mood has flipped toward AI optimism, with S&P 500 futures up about 1.2% and on track for the index's first gain in six sessions, as Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its earlier $70 to $78 range, and Walmart's revenue of $188.8 billion came in just above estimates.

helium.headline: North American Helium's new Stewart Valley plant is producing about 73 million cubic feet a year, and a neighbouring explorer says NAH has recently licensed another well in southwest Saskatchewan.
helium.summary: NAH's Stewart Valley purification facility, which the province calls Canada's largest, came online on September 20, 2026 at roughly 73 million cubic feet of helium per year, and the province says it lifts Saskatchewan's annual output by more than 40 percent. In a November 16 release, partner Helium Evolution said its Glenbain North exploration area lies just south of a well NAH recently licensed at 12-30-16-7W3, one of four areas in its up-to-$3 million winter seismic program. NAH's next big project is a planned helium liquefaction plant in Swift Current, estimated at about $100 million, and a November 17 local report said new federal tax treatment for helium could help it, though some of the company's requests are still under consideration. The market it sells into remains tight: reports this month say spot helium prices have nearly tripled since March amid supply disruptions in Qatar and Russian export limits, and the U.S. designated helium a critical material on October 23.

realestate.headline: Portland-area home prices are holding roughly flat while sales have slowed sharply, with RMLS showing October's metro median at $545,000, up 0.9% from a year ago and closed sales down 21.5%.
realestate.summary: RMLS October figures, as summarized by local brokers, put the Portland metro median sale price at $545,000, up 0.9% from a year earlier and flat from September, while closed sales fell 21.5% year over year. Inventory is about 4.3 months, which brokers describe as balanced but tilting toward buyers. Redfin's city-of-Portland data shows a $525,000 median, up 0.9%, with 1,801 homes sold in October versus 2,079 a year earlier and homes selling in about 26 days. Mortgage rates are easing but still high, with Freddie Mac's 30-year average at 7.11% on November 12 (this week's reading is due later today); none of today's sources broke out North Portland, St. Johns or Sauvie Island.
